outcome: Dysmorphic facial features (slight metopic ridge, ptosis, wide palpebral fissure length, sparse eyebrows, bulbous nose, thin upper lip, full cheeks, small chin, large ears, thin ear helix, prominent antihelix)
Cranial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings (diffusion restriction in supratentorial deep white matter, hypomyelination)
cohort: Two male infants (2.5-month-old and 2-month-old) diagnosed with Combined oxidative phosphorylation deficiency-12 (COXPD12) due to EARS2 gene variants.
finding: Two patients with COXPD12 presented with identical, previously undescribed, dysmorphic facial features alongside neurological findings and lactic acidosis, suggesting these facial features are a key diagnostic clue.
